topic: Coverage record of IMDb's public functionality and information categories (website, apps as described by official help, IMDbPro as a separate professional service), IMDb's data-reuse terms and non-commercial datasets, and openly licensed alternatives (Wikidata, TVmaze) plus restricted ones (TMDB, OMDb) for real-world film/TV metadata
limits: www.imdb.com feature pages (for example /calendar/ and /pressroom/about/) returned HTTP 403 to the fetcher, so the release calendar, charts pages, Awards Central page and press/about pages were not inspected directly. Features are described from help.imdb.com articles only. www.imdb.com/conditions did load.
pro.imdb.com returned HTTP 403. IMDbPro features and pricing come from help.imdb.com IMDbPro articles, not from the marketing site or an account.
No login was used. Nothing behind an IMDb account, the IMDb apps or an IMDbPro subscription was inspected. App behaviour is recorded only as official help pages describe it.
Page text was read through a fetch-and-summarise tool. Quotes are the strings that tool returned in quotation marks. Where it paraphrased instead, confidence is set to medium.

The IMDb Ratings FAQ publishes a Bayesian weighted-rating formula and also says the exact method is not disclosed. Both are recorded. Which charts use the formula, and how the 'regular voter' filter works, are not public.
No dataset file was downloaded. Field lists come from the data.imdb.com documentation page, not from the files themselves.
Prices are USD as shown on the help page on the retrieval date. Regional pricing was not checked.

findings.what: Can SLATE use the IMDb datasets?
findings.value: No, not in a shipped game. The datasets are personal and non-commercial, and IMDb's software policy forbids repurposing them into any movie database other than for one person's own use. A game that bundles or derives a catalogue from them breaks both terms, even if it is free. Commercial use needs a paid licence. FLAG: do not ship IMDb-derived data; use Wikidata (CC0) instead
